scenes.title: Deliver a usable result
scenes.text: A useful handover gives the recipient the right artifact and enough context to use it. A portable document supports continued editing; plain Plant UML source supports text based reuse; images and PDF support reading and presentation. We will preview and download the supported image formats, inspect encoded renderer links, and create local presentation views and review notes. Finish by checking the files you intend to deliver.

scenes.title: Preview and download SVG
scenes.text: Open File, Export and Preview export. Select SVG and inspect the full drawing, margin and background. SVG is useful when a recipient needs a scalable diagram. The export includes the rendered image rather than editor selections and interaction overlays. Check long labels, clipping and authored appearance in the preview before downloading. Keep the file alongside the document so the recipient can distinguish the readable picture from the editable project.

scenes.title: Choose a practical raster scale
scenes.text: Choose PNG for a raster image that can be inserted into many documents. Raster scale changes pixel dimensions and memory use. Increase it only as far as the intended output requires, then inspect readability and the estimated image size. Choose a suitable margin and background. If the app reports an image size limit, reduce scale or use SVG rather than repeatedly attempting an oversized export.

scenes.title: Keep source and copy formats clear
scenes.text: File Export also provides plain source and clipboard formats. Plain source is useful for text workflows, but it does not replace a connected portable document with retained application information. Copy as Markdown and Copy for Confluence prepare content for their destination; review what was copied before pasting it into a shared page. Copying and preparing content do not publish it. Keep private or unfinished work in your practice environment until the intended handover is ready.

scenes.title: Encoded links disclose their source
scenes.text: Link and embed creates an encoded source URL, not a collaboration invitation. Encoding is not encryption: someone with the URL can recover the source. Opening or embedding that URL sends the source to the chosen renderer, and external rendering can differ from this app's local preview. Review the renderer address and disclosure before generating a link. Generating the text locally does not mean the eventual image is an offline artifact.

scenes.title: Present a focused view
scenes.text: Open Presentation and local review from View. Presentation gives the diagram a read only stage with navigation and review tools. Use Fit and zoom for the audience rather than changing task dates to fit a screen. Open the local review panel to choose diagram objects and add highlight steps. A focused explanation should guide the audience through a few meaningful objects, not animate every item simply because it is available.

scenes.title: Keep local views and notes in context
scenes.text: Use a view name to save a meaningful sequence of highlight steps. Choose an object, write a personal review note and anchor it to that object. These views and notes are stored locally in the browser. They are not included in the portable file, exports or live collaboration. Another person will not receive them automatically. Include the required explanation explicitly in your handover, and revisit an anchor if the underlying diagram changes.

scenes.title: Verify and open rendered links
scenes.text: Rendered links are working controls, so review their destinations before opening them. Activate the Portal reference and check the browser confirmation. Cancel this first request and verify that the diagram and source remain unchanged. Accept the second request to open the reference in a separate tab without replacing the editor. The exported SVG also retains the link destination; check the actual artifact when preparing a handover. Web links and mail links use the confirmation guard, while cross diagram member connections and collaboration invitations remain separate features.
scenes.dialogPresentation: Actual native confirmation text is repeated in a labeled overlay; destination content is an actual opened-tab screenshot.

scenes.title: Verify the final package
scenes.text: Finish with a portable project, the required plain source and readable exported diagrams. Reopen the project and inspect connected members, labels, schedule assumptions and retained history. Open the images and PDF at their intended reading size. Include the project start date, status date and important assumptions so a reader can interpret the plan. Document limitations honestly; Jira is excluded from this edition. A good handover makes the next person's first action clear.
